knowledge_base.chunk_text:
Section: Account Takeover (ATO) Playbook — Device Channel > Overview

Detects account takeover attempts through device-related signals.

Section: Account Takeover (ATO) Playbook — Transaction Channel > Overview

Detects account takeover attempts through transaction-related signals.

Section: Account Takeover (ATO) Playbook — Device Channel > Signals

New device: First-time login from an unrecognized deviceEmulator detected: Login from an emulator or virtual deviceDevice fingerprint change: Significant change in device attributes

Section: Account Takeover (ATO) Playbook — Reset Channel > Overview

Detects account takeover attempts through password reset signals.

Section: Account Takeover (ATO) Playbook — Login Channel > Signals

Credential stuffing: 10+ failed logins in a short window, or failure rate >= 0.8Elevated failed logins: 5-9 failed loginsMinor login failures: 1-4 failed loginsNew location: Login from a previously unseen geographic locationNew IP: Login from a previously unseen IP address

Section: Account Takeover (ATO) Playbook — Device Channel > Recommended Actions

New device + emulator: step-up authentication, device challenge, temporary holdNew device only: email verification, notify user of new deviceDevice fingerprint change: monitor for additional signals

Section: Account Takeover (ATO) Playbook — Transaction Channel > Signals

New payee: First-time payment to a new recipientTest payment: Small test payment before larger transferLimit change: Credit/debit limit increase requestCash-out sequence: Rapid movement of funds to external accounts

Section: Account Takeover (ATO) Playbook — Support Channel > Related Playbooks

reset_channel.md — reset signals often come through supportlogin_channel.md — credential stuffing may precede support contact

Section: Account Takeover (ATO) Playbook — Support Channel > Confidence Thresholds

Support takeover pattern: high confidence (>= 0.75)Multiple reset requests: moderate confidence (>= 0.6)Single unusual contact: low confidence (>= 0.4)
